subject: robust fit indices unavailable when intercepts and residuals are set as equal

messages.author: c2c1aa5088b7beb4
messages.subject: robust fit indices unavailable when intercepts and residuals are set as equal
parts:
Dear All, 
Using this code:
config_fapis <- cfa(model_fapis,estimator="WLSMV", data=fapis2, ordered=TRUE, group="group1")

weak_fapis <- cfa(model_fapis,estimator="WLSMV", data=fapis2, ordered=TRUE, group="group1", group.equal="loadings")

strong_fapis<- cfa(model_fapis,estimator="WLSMV", data=fapis2, ordered=TRUE, group="group1", group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"))

strict_fapis<- cfa(model_fapis,estimator="WLSMV", data=fapis2, ordered=TRUE, group="group1", group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts", "residuals"))

I get robust fit indices for configural and weak models (no restrictions and loadings restricted only). Unfortunately, robust fit indices are unavailable for further models (strong and strict, with intercepts and residuals restricted). Do you maybe know why is that?

Maria

messages.author: f6d12b388faad456
messages.subject: Re: robust fit indices unavailable when intercepts and residuals are set as equal
parts:
Hi, Maria,

Not sure if this is the source of your problem, but ordinal variables do not have intercepts and residuals. Strong invariance is tested by restricting the thresholds to be equal. Regarding strict invariance, I've seen two or three papers saying that it is possible to test it with ordinal items, but they never said how. I remember seeing somewhere that you can test it by changing the parameterization to delta, but I've never figured out what changes.

Hope this helps,
Yago

messages.author: f6d12b388faad456
messages.subject: Re: robust fit indices unavailable when intercepts and residuals are set as equal
parts:
Dear Maria,

You are talking about the fit indices that lavaan attach the suffix .robust, right?
I thought lavaan had started to calculate them for WLSMV after an update some time ago, but apparently it is so in some cases only. I tried to do some MG-CFI with ordinal data, and like you, I got these indices for configural and metric invariance, but not for scalar invariance.

Unfortunately, it is beyond my knowledge if this is purposeful or an error. Until recently, we would report the "old robust" indices (lavaan attaches the suffix .scaled to them) when using WLSMV. Maybe you can find an answer in some post about the difference between the scaled and robust statistics, such as this one: https://groups.google.com/u/1/g/lavaan/c/DlVaoP41MyI

I'm sorry for not being more helpful,
Yago

wtorek, 6 czerwca 2023 o 21:16:03 UTC+2 yagol...@gmail.com napisał(a):
Hi, Maria,

Not sure if this is the source of your problem, but ordinal variables do not have intercepts and residuals. Strong invariance is tested by restricting the thresholds to be equal. Regarding strict invariance, I've seen two or three papers saying that it is possible to test it with ordinal items, but they never said how. I remember seeing somewhere that you can test it by changing the parameterization to delta, but I've never figured out what changes.

Hope this helps,
Yago
